newsitem.title: USA: Samsonite sees Q3 restructuring charge.
newsitem.headline: Samsonite sees Q3 restructuring charge.

text.p: Samsonite Corp said on Thursday it would implement a restructuring program to further consolidate operations that would lead to a third-quarter charge of about $10.7 million.
The luggage company said it would save about $0.78 per share, or $12.7 million, in pre-tax savings from the consolidation of operations in North America, Europe and the Far East.
It also plans to eliminate about 450 jobs.

"We are taking advantage of the company's best practices globally to eliminate organizational redundancies throughout the world, and to right-size functional areas and staffing levels. This will significantly improve our cost structure," said Chief Executive Richard Nicolosi.
Samsonite said because it expects to complete the restructuring within the next year, most of the anticipated annual savings will take effect in the fiscal periods starting in November 1997.
The company said about two-thirds of the 450 affected jobs are managerial, office, and clerical positions and about one-third are in operations outside the United States.

The restructuring plan also includes consolidation of hardside luggage production to Samsonite's facility in Denver as well as the eventual shift of many administrative and control functions to the Denver headquarters, Samsonite said.
